options.text: The deployment and management control plane every request goes through

questions.explanation: ARM is Azure's control plane. Requests from the portal, CLI, PowerShell, SDKs, and REST API all go through it for consistent authentication, RBAC, policy, and routing.

questions.prompt: Which statements about resource groups are true? Select all that apply.

options.text: A resource belongs to exactly one resource group at a time
Deleting a resource group deletes everything inside it
A resource group can contain resources from other regions
Resource groups can never be deleted once created

questions.explanation: A resource lives in exactly one group; deleting the group deletes its contents; the group's location only stores metadata, so it can hold resources from other regions. Groups can be deleted.

questions.prompt: Name/value labels you attach to resources to organize them and report on cost are called ____.
questions.explanation: Tags are name/value pairs used to organize, filter, and report on resources (especially cost). They are not inherited by default.

questions.prompt: Order the management hierarchy from broadest to most specific.
questions.explanation: Governance flows management group → subscription → resource group → resource.

questions.prompt: Match each term to its role.

pairs.right: The control plane for all management requests
A label for organizing and cost reporting

questions.explanation: Management groups govern many subscriptions; resource groups contain resources; ARM is the control plane; tags label resources.
